Homage to Hevajra!
The First Chapter:
On the Refutation of the Self (Ātmaparīkṣā)
Thus have I heard at one time: the Blessed One was dwelling upon the bhaga of the Prajñāpāramitā of all the Tathāgatas.

Knowing that he had been entreated by many Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Tathāgatas, and being aware of this as well through the knowledge of the Bodhisattvas, the Blessed One arose from the samādhi of bliss and addressed Vajrapāṇi in this way:
Having washed one's face with water and consumed the medicinal substances,
one should sit upon a comfortable seat and thoroughly accomplish the practice of Heruka.
Visualize at one's own heart the syllable *re pha* blazing like the fire at the end of an eon;
from that arises the Vajrasūrya, perfectly filled with garlands of flames.
Above that is the syllable HŪṂ itself, like the fire at the end of an aeon; having visualized that as a vajra, from that vajra arises Heruka.
Having suppressed the great obstructors, his body is smeared with ashes; perfectly endowed with the five mudrās, he strikes even fear itself with terror.
With hair like the light of sapphire, possessing the strength of a great hero, and endowed with the flavors of the nine dramatic sentiments, he performs the dance with playful movements.
Even the lofty Sumeru, king of mountains, is completely pressed beneath the earth;
having visualized a vajra in one's hand, with the left [hand] holding a human skull-cup—
Visualize it as perfectly endowed with the five nectars and perfectly endowed with the five meats; adorned upon the shoulders by a *khatvāṅga* resembling a jasmine flower, the moon,
and a lotus garland.
This is the first chapter, on the deities, from the Vajrārali.
2. The Second Chapter:
On the Refutation of the Self (Ātman) as a Substance.

Then, all the bodhisattvas headed by Vajrapāṇi; all the Tathāgatas headed by Akṣobhya; all the vajra queens headed by Prajñāpāramitā; all the vajra yakṣas headed by Jambhala; all the bhūtas headed by Śrīmat; all those dwelling in the sky headed by Indra; all the field-protectors headed by Hastikarṇa; all the pretas headed by Kuntadā; and all such sentient beings, through their application of listening to the Dharma, addressed the Great Vajrārāli, the Lord of all Tathāgatas.
"Bhagavān, what is the mantra for the bali offering?
The Bhagavān replied:
"The Teacher of all Sugatas has fully explained the ritual of the bali offering."
The mudrā, moreover, is especially that which accomplishes all desired aims.
With the vajra palms opened upward: Oṃ jvala jvala bhyaḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
This itself is the great mantra; likewise, it is undoubtedly the mantra for the *bali* offering and the mantra for all activities.
This is the second chapter, on the ritual of the *bali* offering from the *Vajrārali*.
The Section on the Path of Cultivation (*bhāvanāmārga*) and the Ultimate Fruition (*niṣṭhāphala*) of the Śrāvaka Vehicle.
Then the Blessed One, having correctly distinguished the names, [spoke of] the samaya:
"If the face is long, it is elevated; likewise, it is like a wish-fulfilling tree."
Abounding in pure conduct, this samaya bestows siddhi.
Having burned lamps made from elephants, donkeys, oxen, and female buffaloes, as well as dogs, and having burned great lamps, one should worship the upholder of the holy life.
The Vow:
Then he proclaimed the vow:
"And living beings are to be slain by you," and so forth.
"You must kill living beings; you must also speak words of falsehood;
you must take what is not given; and you must consort with the wives of others."
The mother, the sister, the daughter, and the granddaughter—
these the knower of yoga should always worship through the ritual of skillful means and wisdom.
Regarding the empowerment:
Then, the command for the empowerment was spoken:
"The master who possesses the mudrā should bestow the empowerment upon him."
Following that empowerment, this very reality is thoroughly distinguished.
That itself is great bliss, abiding pervasively within the body;
this itself is great primordial wisdom, whose nature is supreme joy.
% Homa:
Then, the homa was taught: One should dig into the earth to a depth of one cubit, or half a cubit.
The wise one should prepare the hearth together with white colored powders.

With the mantra as it has been taught, one should certainly perform the fire offering (homa) there with flesh and other substances; for the fire is the very eye of the deity, which accomplishes all desired aims.

*The Definitive Explanation of the Vajrārali*, composed by Śāśvatavajra (Q/R T1410): "The mantrin should dig a pit measuring one cubit, or half a cubit. The wise one should prepare the hearth with very white colored powders (*rajas*). Therein, one should perform the fire offering (*homa*) with meat and other substances, using the recited mantra. The form of one’s own deity is that which accomplishes all desired aims. Thus it is said.
Regarding the drawing of the mandala:
Then the mandala was taught:
it is square with four doors, and beautifully adorned with four archways.
Endowed perfectly with eight pillars, the wise one should draw the mandala.
The wise praise the powder of human bone and pig, as well as the powder of *ldong ros* itself, and even the powder of green substances,
for use within the mandala.
In the center, draw three vajras; at the eastern gate, a large head;
in the south, a vajra bell; likewise, in the west, a battle-axe.
In the north, one should draw a virtuous curved knife within the vajra mandala;
this mandala is fully distinguished for those who desire the meaning of the Dharma and liberation.
Having constructed the mandala, one should then initiate the disciples there; having bound their faces with cloth, one should remove it and show them the mandala.
This is the third chapter, on all activities, from the Vajrārali.

4. The Chapter on the Bodhisattva’s Skillful Means in the Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Flower Ornament Adornment of the Tathāgata’s Wisdom and Virtue, Spoken by the Buddha. Part Four. At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly of bodhisattvas: “O sons of the Buddha, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva wishes to attain the Tathāgata’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, eighteen unique qualities, and all the infinite and boundless buddha-dharmas, they should cultivate the practice of skillful means. What is this practice of skillful means? It is when a bodhisattva, having generated the mind of supreme enlightenment, does not abandon sentient beings, and yet does not dwell upon the characteristics of sentient beings; they do not abandon the path of the bodhisattva, yet do not dwell upon the characteristics of the bodhisattva path; they do not abandon the dharma of the Buddha, yet do not dwell upon the characteristics of the Buddha-dharma. They do not abandon the six perfections, yet do not dwell upon the characteristics of the six perfections. They do not abandon the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, yet do not dwell upon the characteristics of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment. They do not abandon the four foundations of mindfulness, yet do not dwell upon the characteristics of the four foundations of mindfulness. They do not abandon the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, yet they do not dwell upon the characteristics of these dharmas. They do not abandon the ten stages of a bodhisattva, yet do not dwell upon the characteristics of the ten stages. They do not abandon the ten powers, four fearlessnesses, eighteen unique qualities, and all the infinite and boundless buddha-dharmas, yet they do not dwell upon the characteristics of these buddha-dharmas. This is called the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means. The Buddha then spoke a verse to summarize this meaning: “If a bodhisattva wishes to attain the Buddha’s ten powers, The four fearlessnesses, and the eighteen unique qualities, They should cultivate the practice of skillful means. What is the practice of skillful means? It is not abandoning sentient beings, yet not dwelling on their characteristics; Not abandoning the bodhisattva path, yet not dwelling on its characteristics; Not abandoning the Buddha-dharma, yet not dwelling on its characteristics. Not abandoning the six perfections, yet not dwelling on their characteristics; Not abandoning the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, yet not dwelling on their characteristics. Not abandoning the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, The four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, The seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path, Yet not dwelling on the characteristics of these dharmas. Not abandoning the ten stages of a bodhisattva, Yet not dwelling on the characteristics of the ten stages. Not abandoning the ten powers, four fearlessnesses, The eighteen unique qualities, and all the infinite buddha-dharmas, Yet not dwelling on the characteristics of these buddha-dharmas. This is called the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means. At that time, the venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha: “World-Honored One, what is the name of this dharma-door, and how should we uphold it? The Buddha told Śāriputra: “This dharma-door is named ‘The Bodhisattva’s Practice of Skillful Means,’ and you should uphold it by this name. Then the venerable Śāriputra rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and said: “World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door of the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means, how many kinds of roots of goodness will they plant? The Buddha told Śāriputra: “If there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door of the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means, they will plant immeasurable and boundless roots of goodness. Why is this? Because this dharma-door is the source from which all bodhisattvas emerge, and it is the path by which all tathāgatas have attained unexcelled, complete, perfect enlightenment. The Buddha then spoke a verse: “If there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door, The practice of skillful means of the bodhisattvas, They will plant immeasurable and boundless roots of goodness. Why is this? Because this dharma-door is the source of all bodhisattvas, And the path by which all tathāgatas attain supreme enlightenment. At that time, the venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and said: “World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door of the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means, how many kinds of merit will they obtain? The Buddha told Ānanda: “If there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door of the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means, they will obtain immeasurable and boundless merit. Why is this? Because this dharma-door is the treasury of all the virtues of the bodhisattvas and the tathāgatas. The Buddha then spoke a verse: “If there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door, The practice of skillful means of the bodhisattvas, They will obtain immeasurable and boundless merit. Why is this? Because this dharma-door is the treasury of all virtues, Belonging to the bodhisattvas and the tathāgatas. At that time, the venerable Mahākāśyapa rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and said: “World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door of the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means, how many kinds of obstacles will they be able to eliminate? The Buddha told Kāśyapa: “If there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door of the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means, they will be able to eliminate immeasurable and boundless obstacles. Why is this? Because this dharma-door can destroy all the afflictions of the bodhisattvas and the tathāgatas. The Buddha then spoke a verse: “If there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door, The practice of skillful means of the bodhisattvas, They will be able to eliminate immeasurable and boundless obstacles. Why is this? Because this dharma-door can destroy all afflictions, Belonging to the bodhisattvas and the tathāgatas. At that time, the venerable Subhūti rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and said: “World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door of the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means, how many kinds of wisdom will they be able to increase? The Buddha told Subhūti: “If there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door of the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means, they will be able to increase immeasurable and boundless wisdom. Why is this? Because this dharma-door is the mother of all the wisdom of the bodhisattvas and the tathāgatas. The Buddha then spoke a verse: “If there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door, The practice of skillful means of the bodhisattvas, They will be able to increase immeasurable and boundless wisdom. Why is this? Because this dharma-door is the mother of all wisdom, Belonging to the bodhisattvas and the tathāgatas. At that time, the venerable Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and said: “World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door of the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means, how many kinds of compassion will they be able to generate? The Buddha told Pūrṇa: “If there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door of the bodhisattva’s practice of skillful means, they will be able to generate immeasurable and boundless compassion. Why is this? Because this dharma-door is the source from which all the great compassion of the bodhisattvas and the tathāgatas arises. The Buddha then spoke a verse: “If there are sentient beings who hear this dharma-door, The practice of skillful means of the bodhisattvas, They will be able to generate immeasurable and boundless compassion. Why is this? Because this dharma-door is the source of great compassion, Belonging to the
The superknowledges were taught as follows:
the divine eye and the divine ear, the knowledge of others' minds, the recollection of former abodes, and likewise the superknowledge of miraculous powers.
If one meditates on the form of Heruka, the yogi will attain the five superknowledges;
through the yoga of thorough cultivation, one will naturally become Heruka.
Having arisen from meditative concentration, one should thereafter correctly undertake the conduct;
whether the mind is stable or wavering, it is for the sake of inciting one's own mind.
Song is the taking up of various [forms], and likewise, dance is manifoldness itself;
it is the performance of various rituals and the various ornaments upon the body.
Likewise, one should correctly apply oneself to various delightful forms, sounds, as well as smells, tastes, and tangibles.
Then, the Extensive Rituals were proclaimed:
"Having drawn eight squares, one should expand the mantras of the Tantra.
Through the detailed classification of the divisions of activity, likewise [one performs] pacifying, enriching, and so forth."
Oṃ, Ni is in the northeast; likewise, La is in the southeast;
Hūṃ is in the northwest; and Dza is situated in the east.
In the south, it has the form of *dzva*; in the west, the form of *bhyo*;
in the north, with the form of *phaṭ*; and in the center, it abides as *svāhā*.
The name of the object to be accomplished is [inserted] three times.
This is the fourth chapter, the Chapter on Conduct, from the *Vajrārali*.
The Chapter on the True Dharma of the Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Great Vehicle, Entitled "The Lion's Roar" (Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra-bhāṣya, Chapter 5:
Tattvapaṭala).
Regarding the manner of drawing the wheel:
Then, he commanded that the wheel be drawn.

"Kill so-and-so! Subjugate so-and-so! Paralyze so-and-so! Confuse so-and-so! Accomplish everything for so-and-so without exception! Render so-and-so mute! Summon so-and-so! Expel so-and-so! Cause so-and-so to feel hatred! Bind so-and-so! Render so-and-so a eunuch! Render so-and-so hunchbacked! Having written these lines of the mantra on both sides, one should write them with saffron on a leaf of the *gro ga* tree and fasten it to the base of the shoulder.
For summoning, one should draw [the mantra] with lac juice on a cloth stained with menstrual blood.

For rites such as killing and the like, [the substances used are] charcoal from a cremation ground, the juice of *ci-traka*, mustard oil, poison, *ske-tshe*, salt, the three pungent spices (*tsha-ba gsum*), the juice of *ka-na-ka*, and a toothpick made of bone.
For summoning, [use] the thorns of the *āmalaka* fruit.
For one who is deluded, [it is] with dhāruka wood.
For one who is rigid, [it is cured] by the tip of a *vaṭa* branch.
For those who are not spared, one should draw [the figures] with a brush made of bodhivṛkṣa wood.
Now he spoke of the vajra offering, the action seal (*karmamudrā*):
[From] the *Āmnāyamañjarī*:
"Then he spoke of the vajra offering."
In a secluded and solitary place, or within the inner chambers of one's own home,
one should worship a twelve-year-old girl, as well as a sixteen-year-old,
a twenty-five-year-old maiden, a cow, and likewise a buffalo.

One whose self is Heruka should indeed desire a female monkey, a female dog, a female donkey, one born of a camel, a female deer, a female goat, a female pig, or one born of a gavaya; he will attain accomplishment, of this there is no doubt.
Then, he taught the vajra offering:
"In a secluded place at the edge of the earth, or even within one's own home,
for thirteen years, or likewise for sixteen years with a girl..."
The twenty-five to be worshipped are: those born from cows, likewise from female buffaloes,
female yaks, female dogs, female donkeys, likewise female camels, female deer, female goats,
female pigs, and female sheep.
Furthermore, by worshipping Heruka, accomplishment is certain beyond doubt.
On the lunar days when the sun and moon shift, which are designated by the non-Buddhists,
the yogi should taste [the substances] in order to destroy the defilements.
One should not kill living beings; one should not speak words of falsehood;
one should not take what is not given; one should not consort with the wives of others;
one should sleep during the day and rise at night, remaining in a state of profound meditative equipoise.
Great meat and bone, drinking great blood, and truly eating great semen;
likewise, Mahāvairocana himself, the Brahmin woman and the Yaugī woman, the dancer and the smithess.
The skull-bearer woman and the leather-worker, the outcaste as well as the sweeper, the grass-seller and the butcher herself, likewise the barbarian and so forth,
the fowler and the liquor-seller, and furthermore, she who has menstrual flow.
One should not avoid the daughters of one's mother, sister, or daughter; nor should one avoid the daughters born of a wife. One should not take pleasure in the daughters of the *rje’u* caste.
Having always abandoned women who are to be approached, the wise man should resort to those who are not.
This is the fifth chapter, which teaches the magical diagrams (*yantra*) and the action seals (*karmamudrā*) from the *Vajrārali*.

% The Entrustment of the Samaya: Then, the entrustment of the samaya was proclaimed:
"One should not entrust the samaya to those of inferior fortune, such as the śrāvakas."

Likewise, for all those such as the Kṣapaṇakas, the Kapālikas, and the Jaṭilas, one must not instill the awareness of the samaya. If they are masters who possess a nature of compassion, they may be eaten; even if they have attained accomplishment, those of inferior views [must not be].
One who acts for the benefit of sentient beings is called "one of ill fortune";
the Brahmin progenitor is utterly hostile to the samaya.
The Pupil’s Samaya:
Then the samaya of the pupil was proclaimed:
GP 8ab: Steadfast, disciplined, intelligent, patient, upright, and free from deceit.

One who possesses a disciplined mind, is patient, slow-paced, and undeceitful; who is respectful toward the guru and endowed with compassion—such a person’s mental continuum is highly praised in this context.
The Characteristics of the Master:
Next, the characteristics of the master were taught:
"One who knows the application of mantra and tantra, is compassionate, and is skilled in the treatises. (GP 8cd–9ab)
One who thoroughly knows the ten principles, understands the ritual of drawing the mandala,
knows the application of mantra and tantra, possesses compassion, is skilled in the treatises,
fully understands the ten realities, and is expert in the work of painting the mandala.
The Blessing of the Four Sessions:
Then, he taught the blessing of the four sessions:
"By means of that very application of meditation, one first blesses the session."
Then, at whatever time it may be— whether at midday, during the third watch at noon,
or at midnight when free from the [other] times— the consecration of the watches is well known.
Through the yogi’s consecration of the watches, one who possesses the yoga of the self attains accomplishment.
The Mandala of Oneself:
Then, the mandala of oneself was taught:
"Desire, hatred, delusion, envy, and avarice itself."
It does not exist in the Blessed One Heruka; if it were to exist, it would be nothing but purity.
Then, regarding the accomplishment of the samaya, he spoke these words on the accomplishment of the samaya:
One who possesses yoga should accomplish [the practice] upon an obstacle, a planted tree, a hanging tree, or by being struck with a weapon in battle;
this is the internal performance.
Then, he performed the internal activities and spoke these words:
"The precious water for drinking is that which makes one's consumption meaningful;
the immeasurable ablution is performed by means of the vajra, the bell, and so forth, in the sequence of Vairocana."
One should practice the suchness of the samaya-dharma; through the equality of persons,
by this very flavor of the samaya, that which is the very nature of song,
all ḍākinīs are the queens, and [their] sons are Mañjuśrī and the others.
The worshiper of the Wrathful One shall himself become Heruka.
The recitation of the mantra has been correctly explained; the mudrās, such as the *yaṅal* and others, are employed while focusing on the deity yoga, remaining in this state at all times.
What is the use of speaking at length? For one who dwells in the world, in order to attain the state of Vajrasattva, activity itself must be performed through reversal;
for worldly people do not understand activities such as hunting deer and the like.
One who has attained reality practices that which is supremely and most highly praised— the ultimate purity of complete purification.
The Vow: Then the vow was proclaimed:
"One should hold the vajra and bell, and the wise one should consume the nectar."
Constantly relying upon one's own mudrā, one must never transgress the conduct.
Regarding the offering to the deity:
next, the offering to the deity was taught.
In the abode of the forest grove, one should worship oneself as the deity;
one should recite one’s own mantra and consecrate the flowers and other offerings.
This is the sixth chapter, which teaches various activities through the Vajrārali.

7. The Chapter on the Bodhisattva’s Vows and Practices (Bodhisattvacaryāpraṇidhāna-parivarta) At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, having heard these verses spoken by the Buddha Akṣobhya, was filled with great joy and satisfaction. He then addressed the Buddha Akṣobhya: “World-Honored One, I shall go to that Sahā world-system to behold, pay homage to, and serve the Buddha Śākyamuni, as well as to see, pay homage to, and serve those bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who have made such great vows and who practice the bodhisattva path. The Buddha Akṣobhya said to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara: “Good man, you should go at once; it is the proper time. However, good man, when you go to that Sahā world-system, do not disparage the buddha-fields. Why is this? Good man, all buddha-fields possess the same characteristics. Good man, the Sahā world-system is adorned with the seven treasures and is level like the palm of a hand. It is free from pits, thorns, filth, and impurities. There are no mountains such as Mount Sumeru, nor are there mountains of gold, silver, lapis lazuli, mother-of-pearl, agate, red pearl, or emerald. There are no villages, towns, cities, districts, nations, or royal capitals. There are no hells, no realms of animals, and no worlds of Yama. There are no hungry ghosts, no asuras, and no other evil states of existence. The ground is composed of lapis lazuli and is spread with golden sand. There are jeweled trees, and the flowers and fruits are always in season. There are no women in that world; all beings are born through transformation and dwell in palaces made of the seven treasures. They enjoy the pleasures of the five desires and perform the practices of the bodhisattvas. That world is adorned in this way. Furthermore, good man, in that Sahā world-system, the lifespan of sentient beings is immeasurable. Therein, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni constantly teaches the Dharma for the sake of the bodhisattvas, and he rarely teaches the Dharma for the śrāvakas. Why is this? Because in that world, there are many bodhisattvas who have made great vows and who practice the bodhisattva path. Therefore, good man, when you go to that Sahā world-system, you must not disparage the buddha-fields. The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara said to the Buddha Akṣobhya: “World-Honored One, as the Buddha has instructed, I shall not disparage the buddha-fields. Then, the Buddha Akṣobhya, wishing to further explain this matter, spoke these verses: “Go quickly, O son of noble family, To the Sahā world where Śākyamuni dwells. Behold that Buddha, the King of Dharma, And also those sons of the Buddha who have made great vows. Do not disparage the various buddha-fields; All buddhas possess the same characteristics. That world is adorned with the seven treasures, Level and pure, without pits or thorns. There are no mountains such as Sumeru, Nor any mountains of precious gems. There are no villages or towns, Nor any nations or royal capitals. There are no hells or animal realms, Nor any worlds of Yama or hungry ghosts. The ground is made of lapis lazuli, Spread with golden sand and adorned with jewels. There are jeweled trees with seasonal flowers and fruits, And beings dwell in seven-jeweled palaces. They are born by transformation, free from women, Enjoying the pleasures of the five desires. In that world, the lifespan is immeasurable, And the Buddha constantly teaches the bodhisattva path. Therefore, do not disparage that world; All buddha-fields are equal in nature.

Having spoken these verses, the Buddha Akṣobhya again addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara: “Good man, when you go to that Sahā world-system, you should manifest yourself according to the capacities of those sentient beings. If they are capable of seeing a body one fathom tall, you should manifest a body one fathom tall. If they are capable of seeing a body two fathoms tall, you should manifest a body two fathoms tall. If they are capable of seeing a body three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, or even up to a hundred thousand fathoms tall, you should manifest a body of that height. If they are capable of seeing a body one yojana tall, you should manifest a body one yojana tall. If they are capable of seeing a body two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, or even up to a hundred thousand yojanas tall, you should manifest a body of that height. If they are capable of seeing a body half a continent tall, you should manifest a body half a continent tall. If they are capable of seeing a body one continent tall, you should manifest a body one continent tall. If they are capable of seeing a body the size of Jambudvīpa, you should manifest a body the size of Jambudvīpa. If they are capable of seeing a body the size of the four continents, you should manifest a body the size of the four continents. If they are capable of seeing a body the size of a small chiliocosm, you should manifest a body the size of a small chiliocosm. If they are capable of seeing a body the size of a medium chiliocosm, you should manifest a body the size of a medium chiliocosm. If they are capable of seeing a body the size of a great trichiliocosm, you should manifest a body the size of a great trichiliocosm. If they are capable of seeing a body the size of a hundred worlds, you should manifest a body the size of a hundred worlds. Regarding the conduct:
Then the Blessed One spoke regarding the alms-bowl for the collection of food.
As it is said in the *Vajrāraḷi*: "And it has been stated in the *Prakaraṇārthanirṇaya*: [Ms 6v1]... [continues with the citation].
The wise one should wander for alms among the four castes with a broken bowl;
and the learned one should eat on the riverbank from a cracked vessel.
One should eat on the banks of a river and maintain extreme cleanliness.
A wise person should take morsels the size of a parrot’s foot;
one should not eat with the fingers scattered about, nor should one ever accept food from those who do not give it willingly.
To the right, one should circumambulate those who are most devoted from the left;
dwelling in the house without fixed regularity, accomplishment will be attained—of this there is no doubt.
One should fashion a hollow vajra-tree and likewise a bell-tree.
In order to achieve supreme accomplishment, one should always carry it after having grasped it.
Regarding the practice of the Vajra Yakṣiṇī:
then, the practice of the Vajra Yakṣiṇī was taught.
Having taken a tuft of *ser-skya* (yellowish-white) [grass], one should recite this mantra. Having protected it and dried it, one should mix it with *guggulu* (bdellium).
The wise one should first offer incense to the yakṣiṇī with that.
Extremely beautiful and wearing lovely garments, because she is perfectly accomplished within the painted image,
one should summon the yakṣiṇī by means of this very ritual.
Having been given the painted image itself, the yakṣiṇī will come to him.
All of his ornaments— whatever ornaments there may be— should be taken up beforehand; if one so desires,
one should worship with flowers at night.
The Sadhana of the Vajra Vetāla:
Then, the sadhana of the Vajra Vetāla was taught:
"One who is uncut, unwounded, and full should be bathed by one who is well-disciplined."
One should anoint [the site] with great quantities of clarified butter and fumigate it with great incense. To the eastern side of the great mandala, one should offer a lamp of great clarified butter.
Regarding whatever I have instructed you, the mandala should be constructed accordingly.
One should strike the corpse with white mustard seeds and utter the sound "ri bo" loudly;
the wise one should not be afraid of that. One should recite: "Oṃ jvala jvala bhyaḥ hūṃ.
When asked, "What shall I give?", the practitioner should take [it] from her.
The peacock, the eye-salve, the sword, the subterranean realm,
and the pill for traveling through the sky— he will undoubtedly bestow all of these.
[This is] the mandala of the assembly.
Then, he taught the mandala of the gaṇacakra:
"Having performed the aforementioned meditative concentration, one should recite the mantra there.
Through the yoga of oneself as Heruka, one should identify with that very self."
The maṇḍala of the gaṇacakra will be accomplished. In a clean and secluded place, in a peaceful and virtuous location, the yogin should partake [of the feast].
In this very gaṇacakra maṇḍala, of the glorious Heruka—
Regarding the one known as Ārali: while eating, one should engage in conversation;
she dwells upon the head of the King of Mountains, surrounded by a host with pure minds.
Furthermore, she will achieve accomplishment here in this maṇḍala of the assembly, for it is right here that it occurs.
One will not achieve accomplishment through offerings. His queen and protector is Yamāntaka; Prajñāntaka is the lord of his army;
Padmāntaka is the master who guards his body; and Vighnāntaka is his [protector].
He is declared to be the General; known as the King of Desire, he is the Lord of the Protectors of the Face. The glorious Blue Vajra is the Lord of the Gatekeepers; he holds sovereign power over all.
The secondary [deity] is Acala, the Protector himself; the lord of the scribe is likewise Mahābala.
This is the seventh chapter, on the accomplishment of siddhis through the Vajrārali.
Chapter Eight:
The Chapter on the Bodhisattva’s Skillful Means in Cultivating the Perfection of Wisdom.
Playing after attaining the supreme state within the assembly:

Then, having heard this discourse, all [the bodhisattvas] such as Vajrapāṇi completely severed the fetters of existence, became utterly purified, exhausted cyclic existence, and burned away the afflictions.
Then those bodhisattvas addressed these words:
O Vajrārali, you of great diligence! O manifold and marvelous Ema!
You who cover our afflictions and you who bring us to accomplishment!
Then, those bodhisattvas, having attained the supreme excellence of being the best among bipeds, display the play of the Buddhas.
In some [lives] he performed the deeds of perfect enlightenment; in others, he practiced austerities;
there was the emanation of descending from the god realm, as well as the departure from the palace, the turning of the wheel of Dharma, and in some, the act of renouncing the world.
He teaches the Vinaya; his higher mind is the Abhidharma.
In some places he assumes the nature of a Mantra-master; for some, he follows the way of the Pāramitās; for some, the path of the Vaibhāṣikas; and for others, that of the Sautrāntikas.
In some places he is consciousness itself; in some places, he is the Middle Way. In some places he goes to the great hells; in some places he disciplines sentient beings.
Having observed the needs of those to be tamed, he sports with a mind of compassion.
This is the eighth chapter, on the benefits, from the Vajrārali.
The Chapter on the Bodhisattva’s Skillful Means in Purifying the Buddha-field.
Praising the Qualities of the Tantra:
Then, all the Tathāgatas and those Bodhisattvas should teach the analysis of karma.
Whoever observes the samaya within whichever tantra will be praised by all the three worlds.
Whenever one acts with such a continuum, that person will become beautiful in existence.
Whoever makes offerings with song will always possess a melodious voice.
For whoever offers a lamp, that person shall come to possess eyesight.
Whoever performs worship through dance will become a great vidyādhara.
Whoever pays homage to him, to that person the world will pay homage.
Whoever offers fragrant scents will come to possess a body endowed with fragrance.
Whoever offers a beautiful garland will come to possess a golden garland.
Whoever offers garments shall obtain divine robes.
Whoever recites even the mere names, or generates even a slight degree of faith, or develops a superior inclination—
Those people who offer worship—all of them [attain] the most excellent enjoyments of existence, which are utterly pure.
This is the ninth chapter, the Praise of Qualities, from the Vajrārali.
The Chapter on the Bodhisattva’s Lineage and the Ten Grounds (Bodhisattvagotrabhūmidharmaparyāya)
Regarding how a yogi should practice:
furthermore, whoever bestows such completely pure generosity will become the supreme among bipeds.
Then those bodhisattvas, filled with joy yet giving rise to doubt, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, drew near, and asked: "What kind of yoga should we practice?
The Blessed One replied:
One should meditate on Heruka, whose three aspects of giving are completely pure;
Heruka is also the giver, and that to whom one gives is likewise so.
This giving is highly praised. This giving is merely an illustration.
One should practice ethical discipline and so forth in this manner.
Thus it was said in the great king of tantras, the Vajrārali.
The tenth chapter, titled "The Unsurpassed Yoga of the Yoginī" from the Vajrārali, is complete.
